description: Trigger to absolute UTC target instant. Both implementations must agree exactly. A case sets exactly one of expectedTargetInstantUtc (which may be null, meaning an indefinite trigger has no instant) or expectedErrorContains (a substring match, so the two implementations may word a rejection differently while agreeing on the reason).

cases.description: An indefinite keep-awake job has no target instant by design.
A duration is now plus the duration.
The smallest accepted duration still resolves normally.
1440 minutes is exactly 24 hours and is accepted.
A duration is anchored at creation, so the zone must not affect it. Paired with duration-ignores-timezone-newyork: same now, same duration, different zone, identical expected result.
Same inputs as duration-ignores-timezone-saigon but in a DST zone; the target must be identical.
A duration spanning a spring-forward transition adds real elapsed time, not wall-clock time. 23:30 EST on Mar 7 plus 240 minutes lands at 03:30 EDT on Mar 8.
14:00 local Saigon, target 20:00 the same day.
21:00 local Saigon, target 20:00 already passed, so it rolls to tomorrow.
The target must be strictly in the future; a job created at exactly 20:00 for 20:00 must not fire instantly.
One minute before the target, it still resolves to today rather than rolling.
00:00 is a valid wall time and rolls to the next day when already past.
America/New_York 2026-03-08: the clock goes 02:00 to 03:00, so 02:30 does not exist. It must resolve to the instant the clock jumps to, 03:00 EDT.
America/New_York 2026-11-01: the clock goes 02:00 back to 01:00, so 01:30 occurs twice at 05:30Z and 06:30Z. It must resolve to the earlier one.
A zone with a 30-minute offset must resolve correctly. Asia/Kolkata is UTC+5:30, so 22:00 local is 16:30Z.
Asia/Kathmandu is UTC+5:45, an offset that is neither whole nor half hours.
A dated trigger resolves to that exact local date, not to the next occurrence of the time. 20:00 on Aug 10 in Saigon (UTC+7) is 13:00Z, eleven days out from now.

The counterpart of absolute-past-rolls-to-tomorrow: identical now, zone, and time-of-day, plus today's date. The undated form rolls to tomorrow; the dated form must be rejected instead, because moving an irreversible power-off to a day the user did not choose is worse than refusing. This pair is what pins the two semantics apart.
A date wholly in the past is rejected rather than resolved.
The target must be strictly in the future. 20:00 Saigon on Jul 30 is exactly now, so it must be refused rather than firing instantly.
One minute past now is in the future and must be accepted. Paired with absolute-dated-equal-to-now-rejected to pin the boundary from both sides.

A dated trigger resolves the spring-forward gap the same way an undated one does. America/New_York 2026-03-08 has no 02:30, so it resolves to the instant the clock jumps to, 03:00 EDT = 07:00Z. Supplying the date must not open a second resolution path with different DST behaviour.
A dated trigger takes the earlier of an ambiguous wall time, as the undated form does. America/New_York 2026-11-01 01:30 occurs at both 05:30Z and 06:30Z; the earlier is required.

Resolution does not depend on the job type, and the domain places no restriction on a dated keep-awake trigger. Only the desktop UI withholds the control, which is a presentation decision recorded here so it does not read as a domain rule.
